title: Daily BD Actions API
description: Build backend API compatible with the frontend Daily BD Action Suggestion module. Provides async generation of prioritized daily actions, categorized briefing retrieval, action state updates, SSE real-time events, conversational chat, and daily summaries. 7 user stories (P1-P3), 27 FRs, 7 endpoints.

title: Phase 1: Setup & Infrastructure
description: Project initialization: domain models, database migration, repository layer, DI wiring, route registration. Shared infrastructure needed by all user stories.

title: Phase 2: Foundational - Generation Pipeline Core
description: Core generation pipeline service, priority scoring algorithm, and schema DTOs. Must complete before any user story endpoint can work.

title: Phase 3: US1 - Async Daily Actions Generation (P1)
description: POST /v1/daily-actions/generate endpoint. Async Asynq worker. Produces persisted DailyAction records. FR-001 to FR-007.

title: Phase 4: US2 - Read Daily Actions Briefing (P1)
description: GET /v1/daily-actions endpoint. Returns DailyActionsBriefing from DB/cache. FR-008, FR-009.

title: Phase 5: US3 - Update Action State (P1)
description: PATCH /v1/daily-actions/{action_id} endpoint. State transitions, outreach service integration, completion logging. FR-011 to FR-015.

title: Phase 6: US4 - SSE Real-Time Event Stream (P2)
description: GET /v1/daily-actions/events SSE endpoint. SSEManager with Redis pub/sub. Last-Event-ID replay. FR-016 to FR-020.

title: Phase 7: US5 - Category Pagination (P2)
description: GET /v1/daily-actions/categories/{category_id}/actions endpoint. Offset-based pagination. FR-010.

title: Phase 8: US6 - Conversational Chat (P2)
description: POST /v1/daily-actions/chat endpoint. Vercel AI SDK data stream protocol. Intent classification and routing. FR-021 to FR-023.

title: Phase 9: US7 - Daily Summary (P3)
description: GET /v1/daily-actions/summary endpoint. Completion stats, AI-generated narrative. FR-024, FR-025.

title: Phase 10: Polish & Cross-Cutting Concerns
description: Observability (Prometheus metrics, structured logging), performance optimization, documentation, Swagger annotations.

title: T001: Create daily_action domain models
description: Create all domain models for the daily actions feature. These are the foundation for all subsequent layers.
design: Create internal/domain/daily_action/daily_action.go with: DailyActionGeneration, DailyAction, ActionSnooze, ActionCompletionLog, SSEEvent, ChatMessage structs. Create internal/domain/daily_action/enums.go with: ActionType, ActionStatus, CategoryID, GenerationStatus, ActionTransition enums. All models embed base.Base, base.TimestampMixin, base.SoftDeleteMixin. All include UserID uuid.UUID field. Reference: data-model.md for complete struct definitions.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 domain structs compile. All embed required base mixins. All have TableName() methods. Enums match frontend contract types exactly (ActionType: outreach/followup/respond/meeting_prep/enrich; ActionStatus: suggested/in_progress/completed/skipped/snoozed/deferred; CategoryID: replied/followup/new_outreach/meeting_prep/enrichment).

title: T002: Create database migration 000048
description: Create SQL migration files for all 6 new tables needed by the daily actions feature.
design: Create migrations/000048_create_daily_action_tables.up.sql and .down.sql. Tables: daily_action_generations, daily_actions, action_snoozes, action_completion_logs, sse_events, chat_messages. Include all indexes from data-model.md. Use partial indexes with WHERE is_deleted = FALSE where applicable.
acceptance_criteria: make migrate-up succeeds. All 6 tables created with correct columns, types, foreign keys, and indexes. make migrate-down drops all tables cleanly.

title: T003: Create daily_action repository layer
description: Create repositories for all daily action entities following the established GormRepository pattern.
design: Create internal/repository/daily_action/ with: generation_repository.go (FindByUserAndDate, FindByID, Create, UpdateStatus), action_repository.go (FindByGenerationID, FindByID, FindByCategoryWithPagination, UpdateStatus, CountByUserAndDate), snooze_repository.go (Create, ClearByActionID, FindActiveByUserID), completion_log_repository.go (Create, FindByUserAndDate), sse_event_repository.go (Create, FindAfterID), chat_message_repository.go (Create, FindByUserID). All embed gormpkg.GormRepository[T]. All queries scope by UserID.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 repositories compile. All custom queries include UserID scoping. GormRepository[T] base embedded for CRUD. Context propagation via WithContext(ctx).

title: T004: Create request/response schema DTOs
description: Create all request/response DTOs matching the frontend contract exactly.
design: Create internal/schema/v1/daily_action.go with: GenerateRequest, GenerateResponse, DailyActionsBriefingResponse, AgentBriefingSchema, ActionCategorySchema, DailyActionSchema, ActionContactSchema, OutreachActionDataSchema, RespondActionDataSchema, MeetingActionDataSchema, EnrichmentActionDataSchema, UpdateActionRequest, UpdateActionResponse, LoadMoreActionsResponse, DailySummaryResponse, ChatRequest. All field names and JSON tags must match contracts/daily-actions-api.yaml exactly. Use validator struct tags for request validation.
acceptance_criteria: All DTOs compile. JSON tags match the OpenAPI contract field names. Validator tags on required fields. Response structures nest correctly (DailyActionsBriefingResponse contains AgentBriefingSchema, []ActionCategorySchema, PipelineSummarySchema, ActionProgressSchema).

title: T005: Create domain-to-schema mappers
description: Create mappers to convert between domain models and schema DTOs.
design: Create internal/mapper/daily_action.go with functions: MapActionToSchema(domain.DailyAction) -> schema.DailyActionSchema, MapGenerationToBriefing(domain.DailyActionGeneration, []domain.DailyAction) -> schema.DailyActionsBriefingResponse, MapContactToActionContact(contact.Contact) -> schema.ActionContactSchema. Handle JSONB unmarshaling for type-specific data fields (outreach_data, respond_data, meeting_data, enrichment_data).
acceptance_criteria: All mapper functions compile. JSONB fields correctly unmarshaled into typed schema structs. Contact snapshot correctly mapped from domain to schema.

title: T006: Wire dependencies and register routes
description: Add new repositories, services, and handlers to the DI container and register API routes.
design: Update cmd/server/dependencies.go: add DailyActionGenerationRepo, DailyActionRepo, ActionSnoozeRepo, ActionCompletionLogRepo, SSEEventRepo, ChatMessageRepo to Repositories struct. Add DailyActionService to Services struct. Add DailyActionHandler to V1Handlers struct. Initialize in initRepositories, initServices, initV1Handlers. Update cmd/server/routes_v1.go: register dailyActions group under /v1/daily-actions with all 7 endpoints. Service constructor receives: outreach service, all 6 repos, OpenAI client, Redis client, config.
acceptance_criteria: Server compiles and starts with new dependencies. Routes registered at /v1/daily-actions/*. Handler receives all dependencies via constructor injection. No import cycles.

title: T007: Implement priority scoring algorithm
description: Core priority scoring that all action types depend on. Weighted linear additive model producing scores 1-100 (1=highest).
design: Create internal/service/daily_action/priority.go. Implement ComputePriority(contact, outreachState, meeting) -> (score int, factors []PriorityFactor). Weights: response_recency 30%, cadence_deadline 25%, meeting_proximity 25%, data_completeness 12%, lifecycle_stage 8%. Each factor computed on 0-100 urgency scale then inverted. Uses outreach service Config for FU timing windows. Reference: research.md Topic 3 for full computation details.
acceptance_criteria: ComputePriority returns scores 1-100 where 1=highest. Factor breakdown array populated with all 5 factors. A REPLIED contact within 1h scores ~1-5. A COLD PRE_SALES contact with no meeting scores ~50-70. Edge cases: nil meeting returns 0 for proximity factor, nil outreach state returns neutral scores.

title: T008: Implement generation pipeline service
description: Core service that orchestrates the generation pipeline: fetches contacts, determines states, scores priorities, generates drafts, creates persisted DailyAction records.
design: Create internal/service/daily_action/service.go with Service struct. Constructor receives: outreach service, all repos, OpenAI client, Redis client. Implement GenerateActions(ctx, userID, language, forceRefresh) method that: (1) creates DailyActionGeneration record with status=started, (2) calls outreach.SuggestContacts for all active contacts, (3) for each contact calls DetermineConversationState, (4) maps state to action type and category, (5) calls ComputePriority, (6) generates draft via GenerateDraftForHandlerWithLanguage (for outreach/followup), (7) generates meeting prep via GenerateMeetingPrep (for meeting_prep), (8) identifies missing fields (for enrich), (9) creates DailyAction records in DB, (10) generates AgentBriefing via OpenAI, (11) updates generation status to ready. This is called by the Asynq worker.
acceptance_criteria: GenerateActions creates DailyActionGeneration and DailyAction records. Each action has correct type, category, priority, contact snapshot, and type-specific data. Generation status transitions: started -> generating -> ready. Returns generation_id and action_count.

title: T009: Create daily_action handler with endpoint stubs
description: HTTP handler with all 7 endpoint methods. Stubs can return 501 initially; each user story phase fills in the implementation.
design: Create internal/handler/v1/daily_action/handler.go. Handler struct receives DailyActionService, AuthHelper, ResponseHelper. Methods: Generate(c fiber.Ctx) error, GetDailyActions(c fiber.Ctx) error, UpdateAction(c fiber.Ctx) error, SSEStream(c fiber.Ctx) error, GetSummary(c fiber.Ctx) error, LoadMoreActions(c fiber.Ctx) error, Chat(c fiber.Ctx) error. Each extracts userID via authHelper, parses request, delegates to service, maps response, returns via responseHelper.
acceptance_criteria: Handler compiles. All 7 methods registered in routes. Auth middleware applied. Each method extracts userID correctly. Request binding uses c.Bind().JSON() for POST/PATCH, c.Query() for GET params.

title: T010: Implement Asynq generation worker
description: Background worker that executes the generation pipeline asynchronously when triggered by POST /generate.
design: Create internal/worker/daily_action/generation_worker.go. Define task type constant 'daily_action:generate'. Worker struct receives DailyActionService. HandleGenerateActions(ctx, task) unmarshals payload (userID, language, forceRefresh), calls service.GenerateActions, publishes generation_complete SSE event on success. Register in cmd/worker/main.go with default queue priority. Create internal/worker/dto/daily_action.go with GenerateActionsPayload struct.
acceptance_criteria: Worker registered in cmd/worker/main.go. Accepts daily_action:generate tasks. Calls GenerateActions service method. Publishes generation_complete event via Redis pub/sub on completion. Logs task type, user_id, and outcome per constitution.

title: T011: Implement POST /generate endpoint
description: Implement the Generate handler method to accept generation requests and enqueue Asynq tasks.
design: In handler.go Generate method: (1) extract userID, (2) parse GenerateRequest body (language, force_refresh), (3) check if generation already in progress via repo.FindByUserAndDate with status=started/generating -> return 429, (4) check if cached generation exists and not stale and not force_refresh -> return 202 with cached generation_id, (5) otherwise enqueue Asynq task with daily_action:generate type, (6) return 202 with generation_id and status. Use ResponseHelper for standardized APIResponse wrapper.
acceptance_criteria: POST /v1/daily-actions/generate returns 202 within 200ms. Returns generation_id and generation_status (started/already_in_progress/cached). 429 when generation in progress. Accepts language and force_refresh params. Asynq task enqueued on new generation.

title: T012: Implement generation staleness detection
description: Detect when generation results become stale due to new events (prospect replies, meeting changes) since last generation.
design: Add method to service: CheckStaleness(ctx, userID, generationID) bool. Check if any new interactions (via interactionRepo.HasIncomingAfter), new meetings, or contact status changes occurred after generation.GeneratedAt. If stale, update generation status to 'stale'. Called by GET /daily-actions before returning results.
acceptance_criteria: Generation status transitions to stale when new events detected since generated_at. GET /daily-actions returns generation_status: stale when applicable. force_refresh=true triggers new generation even with stale results.

title: T013: Implement GET /daily-actions endpoint
description: Implement the GetDailyActions handler that returns the full DailyActionsBriefing from DB.
design: In handler.go GetDailyActions method: (1) extract userID, (2) parse query params (language, include_completed), (3) find latest non-replaced generation via generationRepo.FindByUserAndDate, (4) if none return generation_status: not_generated with empty categories, (5) check staleness via T012, (6) load actions grouped by category (first 5 per category, sorted by priority ASC), (7) build AgentBriefing from generation.AgentBriefing JSONB, (8) compute progress (total, completed, skipped, snoozed, remaining), (9) build PipelineSummary from generation.PipelineSummary JSONB, (10) map to DailyActionsBriefingResponse, (11) filter out completed if include_completed=false. Use mapper functions from T005.
acceptance_criteria: GET /v1/daily-actions returns 200 within 500ms. Response matches DailyActionsBriefing schema exactly. generation_status reflects not_generated/generating/ready/stale. Categories ordered as replied, followup, new_outreach, meeting_prep, enrichment. Each category has max 5 actions with has_more and next_offset. Progress counters accurate. include_completed=false filters correctly.

title: T014: Implement AI agent briefing generation
description: Generate the AgentBriefing during the generation pipeline: AI-generated greeting, strategic reasoning with memory references, and category counts.
design: Add to internal/service/daily_action/briefing.go: GenerateAgentBriefing(ctx, userID, actions []DailyAction, language) -> AgentBriefing. Uses OpenAI GPT-4o-mini with a system prompt that: describes the BD rep's pipeline state, lists today's actions by category, references recent notable events (replies, meetings). Returns greeting (time-appropriate), strategic_reasoning (narrative), memory_references (array of contact events), category_counts. Also implement GeneratePipelineSummary(ctx, userID) -> PipelineSummary using contact repo queries.
acceptance_criteria: AgentBriefing contains non-empty greeting, strategic_reasoning, memory_references array, and category_counts array. Language parameter controls output language (vi/en). Pipeline summary includes accurate counts from DB.

title: T015: Implement PATCH /{action_id} endpoint
description: Implement action state transitions: mark_sent, skip, snooze, snooze_custom, mark_completed, reopen.
design: In handler.go UpdateAction method: (1) extract userID and action_id from path, (2) parse UpdateActionRequest (transition, content, channel, skip_reason, snooze_until, feedback_action), (3) find action by ID and verify ownership, (4) validate transition against current status (see state machine in data-model.md), (5) delegate to service method ExecuteTransition(ctx, action, request). Service handles each transition type differently. Return 404 if not found, 409 if invalid transition.
acceptance_criteria: PATCH returns updated action, contact_state_change (if applicable), and progress. All 6 transitions work correctly. 404 for unknown action_id. 409 for invalid state transitions. Response within 500ms.

title: T016: Implement mark_sent transition with outreach integration
description: mark_sent transition: log interaction, advance contact state, record feedback, return state change.
design: In service, ExecuteMarkSent(ctx, action, content, channel, feedback): (1) call outreach.UpdateOutreachForHandler with event=sent, (2) record feedback via outreach.RecordAction, (3) update action status to completed, (4) create ActionCompletionLog entry, (5) return contact_state_change with previous/new state. Map feedback from daily actions format to outreach feedback format.
acceptance_criteria: mark_sent logs interaction via outreach service. Contact state advances (e.g., COLD -> NO_REPLY). Feedback recorded. ActionCompletionLog created. contact_state_change included in response.

title: T017: Implement snooze system
description: Snooze and snooze_custom transitions: store reappearance time, exclude from active lists.
design: In service, ExecuteSnooze(ctx, action, snoozeUntil *time.Time): (1) determine snooze time (default 5pm user timezone from profile, UTC if unknown; use custom time if provided), (2) create ActionSnooze record, (3) update action status to snoozed and set snooze_until, (4) create ActionCompletionLog entry. For reopen: clear snooze via snoozeRepo.ClearByActionID (set cleared_at), reset action status to suggested. Query-time filtering: when fetching active actions, exclude where status=snoozed AND snooze_until > NOW().
acceptance_criteria: Snooze creates ActionSnooze record. Default time is 5pm user timezone. Custom snooze_until respected. Snoozed actions excluded from active lists. Reopen clears snooze and returns to suggested. ActionCompletionLog created for both snooze and reopen.

title: T018: Implement skip and mark_completed transitions
description: Skip (with optional reason) and mark_completed (for meeting_prep, enrich) transitions.
design: In service: ExecuteSkip(ctx, action, reason) updates status to skipped, records skip_reason in ActionCompletionLog. ExecuteMarkCompleted(ctx, action) updates status to completed, creates ActionCompletionLog. Both update progress counters. No outreach service interaction for these transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Skip records optional reason. mark_completed works for meeting_prep and enrich action types. Both create ActionCompletionLog entries. Progress counters updated correctly.

title: T019: Implement SSEManager with Redis pub/sub
description: SSE connection registry with Redis pub/sub for cross-instance event delivery.
design: Create internal/service/daily_action/sse_manager.go. SSEManager struct with: connections map[uuid.UUID][]chan *SSEEvent, sync.RWMutex, Redis client, Redis PubSub. Methods: NewSSEManager(redisClient), Register(ctx, userID) chan *SSEEvent, Unregister(userID, ch), PublishEvent(ctx, userID, event), Close(). Redis channels: sse:daily-actions:{user_id}. Buffer size: 64 events per channel. Pattern follows existing WebSocketManager at internal/handler/v1/pubsub/websocket_manager.go. Reference: research.md Topic 1.
acceptance_criteria: SSEManager registers/unregisters per-user connections. PublishEvent delivers to all local connections for that user. Redis pub/sub enables cross-instance delivery. Thread-safe with RWMutex. Graceful cleanup on Close().

title: T020: Implement GET /events SSE endpoint
description: SSE streaming endpoint using Fiber's SetBodyStreamWriter.
design: In handler.go SSEStream method: (1) extract userID BEFORE entering stream writer, (2) read Last-Event-ID header, (3) set headers (Content-Type: text/event-stream, Cache-Control: no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering: no), (4) c.RequestCtx().SetBodyStreamWriter(func(w *bufio.Writer)): register with SSEManager, replay missed events if Last-Event-ID provided, send retry:3000, heartbeat every 15s, select on event channel and heartbeat ticker, detect disconnect via w.Flush() error. Wire SSEManager in dependencies.go.
acceptance_criteria: GET /v1/daily-actions/events opens SSE stream. Events arrive in id/event/data SSE format. Heartbeat every 15s keeps connection alive. Flush errors close connection gracefully. Last-Event-ID replays missed events from Redis sorted set.

title: T021: Implement SSE event producers
description: Wire event producers: generation_complete, action_updated, snooze_expired. prospect_replied and meeting_approaching depend on existing notification pipelines.
design: generation_complete: published by generation worker (T010) after successful generation. action_updated: published by UpdateAction handler (T015) after state change. snooze_expired: schedule Asynq delayed task at snooze_until time that publishes event. prospect_replied: hook into existing gmail notification worker to publish SSE event when reply detected (add SSEManager dependency to gmail worker). meeting_approaching: add a periodic Asynq task that checks for meetings within 2h and publishes events. followup_due: check during generation or as periodic task. Each event persisted in Redis sorted set (sse:events:{user_id}, 5-min TTL) for replay.
acceptance_criteria: generation_complete fires when generation finishes. action_updated fires on PATCH. snooze_expired fires at correct time. Events persisted in Redis for 5-min replay window. All event payloads match frontend SSE event type schemas.

title: T022: Implement GET /categories/{id}/actions endpoint
description: Offset-based pagination for loading more actions within a category.
design: In handler.go LoadMoreActions method: (1) extract userID, category_id from path, (2) parse offset and limit from query (default limit=5), (3) validate category_id against known CategoryID enum, (4) query actionRepo.FindByCategoryWithPagination(ctx, userID, generationID, categoryID, offset, limit+1) - fetch limit+1 to determine has_more, (5) map to LoadMoreActionsResponse with actions, has_more, next_offset. Repo query: WHERE user_id=? AND generation_id=? AND category_id=? AND status=suggested AND is_deleted=false ORDER BY priority ASC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?.
acceptance_criteria: GET /categories/{id}/actions returns paginated actions sorted by priority. has_more true when more exist. next_offset calculated correctly. Returns 400 for invalid category_id. Response within 200ms.

title: T023: Implement chat intent classifier
description: Classify user messages into intent categories and route to appropriate handlers.
design: Create internal/service/daily_action/chat.go. ChatService struct with OpenAI client, daily action service, contact repo. ClassifyIntent(ctx, message) -> (intent string, entities []string). Intents: action_command (mark sent, regenerate, skip), pipeline_query (reply rate, contact filter), strategy_query (approach recommendation), analytics_request (summary, metrics), contact_lookup. Use GPT-4o-mini with a classification prompt. When entities are ambiguous, return disambiguation options.
acceptance_criteria: Intent classification returns correct category for: action commands, pipeline queries, strategy questions, analytics requests, contact lookups. Disambiguation triggered when multiple contacts match a name. Vietnamese and English input supported.

title: T024: Implement POST /chat streaming endpoint
description: Chat endpoint that streams responses using the Vercel AI SDK data stream protocol.
design: In handler.go Chat method: (1) extract userID, (2) parse ChatRequest (messages array), (3) save user message to chat_messages table, (4) set response headers: Content-Type text/plain; charset=utf-8, X-Vercel-AI-Data-Stream v1, (5) c.RequestCtx().SetBodyStreamWriter: classify intent via ChatService, build system prompt with pipeline context, call OpenAI CreateChatCompletionStream, write f:{messageId} start, for each token write 0:{json text}, write e:{finishReason} and d:{finishReason}, save assistant message to chat_messages. Flush after each line. Reference: research.md Topic 2 for exact wire format.
acceptance_criteria: POST /chat returns streamed response in Vercel AI SDK format (code:json lines). First token within 2s. Correct headers (text/plain, X-Vercel-AI-Data-Stream: v1). Messages saved to chat_messages table. Intent classification informs response context.

title: T025: Implement GET /summary endpoint
description: Daily progress summary with completion stats, breakdown, outcomes, carry-over, and AI narrative.
design: In handler.go GetSummary method: (1) extract userID, parse language query param, (2) query today's ActionCompletionLog entries grouped by transition type, (3) compute progress (total, completed, skipped, snoozed, remaining, completion_rate), (4) compute breakdown (outreach_sent, followups_sent, replies_handled, meetings_prepped, contacts_enriched), (5) compute outcomes from today's new interactions (responses received, meetings booked, contacts dropped), (6) find carry_over (actions not completed: snoozed past time, not addressed), (7) generate agent_summary via OpenAI (celebrate wins, flag concerns). Return DailySummaryResponse.
acceptance_criteria: GET /summary returns within 500ms. Progress counters accurate. Breakdown by action type correct. Carry-over includes uncompleted actions with reason. agent_summary is AI-generated narrative. Language param controls output.

title: T026: Add Prometheus metrics for daily actions
description: Observability: Prometheus counters/histograms for all daily action operations.
design: Add metrics in internal/service/daily_action/service.go and handler: (1) http_daily_actions_request_duration_seconds histogram by endpoint, (2) daily_actions_generation_duration_seconds histogram, (3) daily_actions_generation_action_count gauge, (4) daily_actions_sse_connections_active gauge, (5) daily_actions_chat_ttft_seconds histogram, (6) daily_actions_transitions_total counter by transition type. Use existing pkg/metrics/ patterns.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 metrics registered and exported. Generation duration tracked. SSE connection count accurate. Chat TTFT measured. Transition counts by type available.

title: T027: Add structured logging throughout
description: Ensure all service/worker/handler methods have structured zerolog logging per constitution.
design: Review all created files. Each handler method logs: request received (Info), user_id, action taken. Service methods log: generation started/completed with action_count, transition executed with action_id. Worker logs: task received, payload summary, outcome. Use .With() for structured fields. Include request_id where available.
acceptance_criteria: All handler, service, and worker methods have appropriate log statements. Structured fields include user_id, action_id, generation_id. Log levels appropriate (Info for operations, Error for failures, Debug for diagnostics).

title: T028: Add Swagger annotations
description: Add Swagger/OpenAPI annotations to all handler methods for documentation generation.
design: Add swaggo annotations to each handler method in internal/handler/v1/daily_action/handler.go following existing patterns from outreach handler. Run make swagger to regenerate docs.
acceptance_criteria: make swagger generates documentation including all 7 daily action endpoints. Annotations match contract schemas.

title: v3 Frontend Compatibility Fixes
description: Fix 6 response shape mismatches between backend API and frontend TypeScript types identified during integration testing. Gaps: (1) category_counts.color missing, (2) categories icon/color/description not populated, (3) generated_at not set, (4) pipeline_summary not computed, (5) chat returns plain JSON instead of Vercel AI SDK streaming, (6) SSE Last-Event-ID replay not implemented.

title: Phase 1: Response Shape Fixes (Gaps 1,2,3)
description: Fix missing fields in GET /daily-actions response: category_counts[].color, categories[].icon/color/description, generated_at, completion_rate. All are simple field additions or metadata mappings — no new architecture.

title: Phase 2: Pipeline Summary (Gap 4)
description: Compute and return pipeline_summary in the briefing response. Requires new BuildPipelineSummary() service method that queries contacts by stage, computes 7-day metrics, and integrates into GetDailyActions handler.

title: Phase 3: Chat Streaming Rewrite (Gap 5)
description: Rewrite POST /chat handler from plain JSON response to Vercel AI SDK data stream protocol (code:json\n format). Requires SetBodyStreamWriter, OpenAI streaming API, and correct framing (f:, 0:, e:, d: lines).

title: Phase 4: SSE Last-Event-ID Replay (Gap 6)
description: Implement missed event replay in SSEStream handler. On reconnect with Last-Event-ID header, query SSEEventRepository.FindByUserSince() for missed events and replay them before entering the live event loop.

title: T029: Add Color field to CategoryCount domain and schema
description: Frontend expects category_counts[].color (string) for badge styling. Currently missing from both the domain CategoryCount struct and schema CategoryCountResponse.
design: 1. In internal/domain/daily_action/daily_action.go line 174-179, add 'Color string `json:"color"`' to CategoryCount struct after Icon field. 2. In internal/schema/v1/daily_action.go line 78-83, add 'Color string `json:"color"`' to CategoryCountResponse struct after Icon field. Both changes are single-line additions.
acceptance_criteria: CategoryCount domain struct has Color string field with json:"color" tag. CategoryCountResponse schema struct has matching Color field. Both compile. Existing JSONB data without color field unmarshals cleanly (Color defaults to empty string).

title: T030: Update mapper and briefing to include color
description: AgentBriefingToResponse mapper at internal/mapper/daily_action.go line 103-111 maps CategoryCounts but doesn't include the Color field. Also, briefing generation in service should produce color values for each category.
design: 1. In internal/mapper/daily_action.go AgentBriefingToResponse(), add 'Color: c.Color' to the CategoryCountResponse mapping at line 109. 2. In internal/service/daily_action/briefing.go, update the briefing generation to include color for each category count. Use category metadata: replied=green, followup=orange, new_outreach=blue, meeting_prep=purple, enrichment=red.
acceptance_criteria: AgentBriefingToResponse maps Color field from domain to schema. Generated briefings include color values for each category. Response JSON includes non-empty color strings matching the metadata map.

title: T031: Add category metadata in GetDailyActions handler
description: Categories in the briefing response have empty icon, color, and description fields because the handler doesn't populate them. Frontend requires these for rendering category headers.
design: In internal/handler/v1/daily_action/handler.go GetDailyActions() method, add a categoryMetadata map alongside the existing categoryLabels map (line 231-237). Map: replied -> {icon: "💬", color: "green", description: "Prospects who replied to your outreach"}, followup -> {icon: "⏰", color: "orange", description: "Follow-ups due based on your cadence"}, new_outreach -> {icon: "📤", color: "blue", description: "New contacts ready for first outreach"}, meeting_prep -> {icon: "📅", color: "purple", description: "Upcoming meetings needing preparation"}, enrichment -> {icon: "🔍", color: "red", description: "Contacts with missing data to enrich"}. Then at lines 255-262 where ActionCategoryResponse is built, set Icon, Color, Description from the metadata map.
acceptance_criteria: Each ActionCategoryResponse in the GET /daily-actions response includes non-empty icon (emoji), color (string), and description fields matching the category metadata table in data-model.md.

title: T032: Set generated_at and completion_rate in briefing response
description: generated_at is always null in the response even when generation is ready. completion_rate is always 0. Frontend needs both for display.
design: In internal/handler/v1/daily_action/handler.go GetDailyActions() at lines 294-308: 1. Set GeneratedAt from gen.GeneratedAt (already available on the generation domain model at domain line 22). Add 'GeneratedAt: gen.GeneratedAt' to the DailyActionsBriefing struct literal. 2. Compute CompletionRate: if total > 0, completionRate = float64(completed) / float64(total). Add 'CompletionRate: completionRate' to the ActionProgressResponse struct literal at line 306.
acceptance_criteria: When generation_status is 'ready', generated_at is non-null ISO8601 timestamp in the response. completion_rate is a float between 0 and 1 reflecting completed/total ratio. When no actions exist, completion_rate is 0.

title: T033: Implement BuildPipelineSummary service method
description: Frontend expects pipeline_summary with 6 fields but backend never computes it. Need a new service method that queries contact and interaction data to build the summary.
design: Add method to internal/service/daily_action/service.go: BuildPipelineSummary(ctx context.Context, userID uuid.UUID) (*v1.PipelineSummaryResponse, error). Implementation: (1) Query contact repo for active contacts by user -> total_active_contacts. (2) GROUP BY outreach_stage -> contacts_by_stage map[string]int. (3) GROUP BY lifecycle_stage -> contacts_by_lifecycle map[string]int. (4) Query interactions from last 7 days: count replies / count outgoing = response_rate_7d. (5) Count meetings booked in last 7 days -> meetings_booked_7d. (6) Avg time between outgoing message and first reply in last 7 days -> avg_response_time_hours. Use existing outreach repository and contact repository methods. If a query fails, use 0 as default rather than failing the whole summary.
acceptance_criteria: BuildPipelineSummary returns a populated PipelineSummaryResponse with all 6 fields. total_active_contacts counts non-deleted contacts. contacts_by_stage and contacts_by_lifecycle are maps with string keys and int values. 7-day metrics computed from interaction records. Returns gracefully with zeros if no data.

title: T034: Integrate pipeline_summary into GetDailyActions handler
description: Call BuildPipelineSummary from GetDailyActions handler and include result in the briefing response.
design: In internal/handler/v1/daily_action/handler.go GetDailyActions() method, before building the final response (line 294): (1) Call h.service.BuildPipelineSummary(ctx, userID). (2) If error, log warning and continue with nil pipeline_summary (non-critical). (3) Add PipelineSummary field to the DailyActionsBriefing response struct literal at line 294.
acceptance_criteria: GET /daily-actions response includes non-null pipeline_summary when generation is ready. pipeline_summary contains all 6 fields matching PipelineSummaryResponse schema. If computation fails, response still returns successfully with null pipeline_summary.

title: T035: Rewrite Chat handler to Vercel AI SDK streaming protocol
description: Current Chat handler returns plain JSON {role, content}. Frontend useChat() hook expects Vercel AI SDK data stream protocol with text/plain content type and code:json line format.
acceptance_criteria: POST /chat returns Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8 and X-Vercel-AI-Data-Stream: v1 headers. Response body follows code:json\n format. Starts with f: frame, streams 0: text chunks, ends with e: and d: frames. Frontend useChat() hook renders streamed tokens correctly. Messages still saved to chat_messages table.

title: T036: Implement SSE Last-Event-ID replay
description: SSEStream handler reads the Last-Event-ID header on reconnect but doesn't query for missed events. Frontend EventSource expects missed events to be replayed.
design:
In internal/handler/v1/daily_action/handler.go SSEStream() method (lines 460-519), after registering with SSEManager (line 483) and inside the SetBodyStreamWriter callback (line 485): (1) Read Last-Event-ID header: lastEventID := c.Get("Last-Event-ID"). Note: must read the header BEFORE entering SetBodyStreamWriter since c is not safe inside the callback. Pass it as a closure variable. (2) After writing retry:3000 (line 491), if lastEventID is non-empty: parse it as UUID, call h.sseEventRepo.FindByUserSince(ctx, userID, parsedUUID), iterate the returned events and write each as SSE: fmt.Fprintf(w, "id: %s
event: %s
data: %s

", event.ID, event.EventType, string(event.Payload)), then w.Flush(). (3) If parse fails or repo returns error, log warning and continue without replay (graceful degradation). The SSEEventRepository.FindByUserSince() method already exists and returns events created after the reference event's timestamp.
acceptance_criteria: When client reconnects with Last-Event-ID header, missed events are replayed in chronological order before live events. If Last-Event-ID is not a valid UUID or event not found, stream starts fresh without error. Events are replayed in the same SSE format (id/event/data). Live event loop continues after replay.
